en: Udāna 5.6 Soṇasutta Thus have I heard:
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Mahākaccāna was dwelling among the Avantīs at Kuraraghara on Mount Pavatta.
At that time, the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa was the attendant of the Venerable Mahākaccāna.
Then, while the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind:

“In whatever way the noble Mahākaccāna teaches the Dhamma, it is not easy for one living at home to lead the holy life in its absolute fullness, absolute purity, and total perfection, like a polished shell.
What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, put on saffron robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?”
Then the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa approached the Venerable Mahākaccāna; having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahākaccāna and sat down to one side.
As he was sitting there, the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa said this to the Venerable Mahākaccāna:
"Here, Bhante, while I was alone in seclusion, a reflection arose in my mind thus: [text continues]"
“In whatever way the venerable Mahākaccāna teaches the Dhamma, it is not easy for one living at home to lead the holy life in its entirety, perfectly pure, polished like a conch shell.
What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, put on saffron robes, and go forth from the home life into homelessness?
“Venerable sir, let the venerable Mahākaccāna ordain me.”
When this was said, the Venerable Mahākaccāna said to the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa:
“It is indeed difficult, Soṇa, to practice the holy life for as long as life lasts with a single meal and a single bed.
Come now, Soṇa, while remaining a householder, apply yourself to the teaching of the Buddhas by practicing a timely single meal and a single bed.”
Then the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa’s intention for the going forth subsided.
A second time...
[as before] ...a second time the Venerable Mahākaccāna said this to the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa:
“Indeed, Soṇa, it is difficult to practice the holy life of eating one meal a day and sleeping alone for as long as life lasts.
Come now, Soṇa, while remaining a householder, apply yourself to the teaching of the Buddhas by practicing at the appropriate time the holy life of eating one meal a day and sleeping alone.
For a second time, the aspiration for the going forth that had arisen in the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa subsided.
A third time, while the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind:
"In whatever way the noble Mahākaccāna teaches the Dhamma, it is not easy for one living at home to practice the holy life in its absolute fullness, absolute purity, and polished perfection.
What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, put on saffron robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?"
A third time, the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa approached the Venerable Mahākaccāna; having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahākaccāna and sat down to one side.
As he was sitting there, the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa said this to the Venerable Mahākaccāna:
"Venerable sir, as I was here alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in my mind: [text continues]"

“In whatever way the venerable Mahākaccāna teaches the Dhamma, it is not easy for one living at home to lead the holy life in its complete perfection, in its total purity, polished like a conch shell.
What if I were to shave off my hair and beard, don the saffron robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness?
“Venerable sir, let the venerable Mahākaccāna ordain me.”
Then the Venerable Mahākaccāna gave the going-forth to the lay follower Soṇa Kuṭikaṇṇa.
Now at that time, the region of Avanti in the southern province had few bhikkhus.

Then, after three years had passed, the Venerable Mahākaccāna—with great difficulty and hardship—having gathered a quorum of ten bhikkhus from here and there, conferred full ordination upon the Venerable Soṇa.
Then, as the Venerable Soṇa had completed the rains retreat, while he was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind:
"I have not seen that Blessed One face-to-face; however, I have merely heard it said:
'That Blessed One is such and such.'"
“If my preceptor would grant me permission, I would go to see that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
Then, in the evening, the Venerable Soṇa emerged from seclusion and approached the Venerable Mahākaccāna. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Mahākaccāna and sat down to one side.
Sitting there, the Venerable Soṇa said this to the Venerable Mahākaccāna:
“Here, venerable sir, while I was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in my mind:
‘I have not seen that Blessed One face-to-face; however, I have merely heard:
“That Blessed One is such and such”’.”
“If my preceptor would grant me permission, I would go to see that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
“Excellent, excellent, Soṇa!
Go, Soṇa, to see that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.”

"You will see, Soṇa, that Blessed One who is inspiring, inspiring to behold, with tranquil faculties and a tranquil mind, who has attained the highest self-control and composure, who is tamed, guarded, with senses restrained—a true elephant.

Having seen him, pay homage at the Blessed One’s feet in my name, and inquire after his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, physical lightness, strength, and well-being, saying: [‘Is the Blessed One free from illness... and living in comfort?’]"

“Venerable sir, my preceptor, the Venerable Mahākaccāna, pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet; he inquires after your health, freedom from illness, physical lightness, strength, and well-being.

“So be it, venerable sir,” the Venerable Soṇa replied, and having rejoiced and expressed his appreciation for the Venerable Mahākaccāna’s words, he rose from his seat, paid homage to the Venerable Mahākaccāna, circumambulated him keeping him to his right, and tidied his lodging.
Taking his bowl and robe, he set out on a wandering tour toward Sāvatthī.

Traveling by stages on his tour, he eventually reached Sāvatthī, the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery, where the Blessed One was staying. Having approached the Blessed One and paid homage to him, he sat down to one side.
As he was sitting there, the Venerable Soṇa said this to the Blessed One:

“Venerable sir, my preceptor, the Venerable Mahākaccāna, pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet; he asks after your health, your freedom from affliction, your lightness of being, your strength, and your well-being.
“Bhikkhu, I hope you are enduring, I hope you are getting by, I hope you have come along the road without too much fatigue, and that you are not distressed for alms?
“It is endurable, Blessed One; it is getting by, Blessed One. And I, venerable sir, have come along the road without too much fatigue, nor am I distressed for alms.”
Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
“Ānanda, prepare a lodging for this visiting bhikkhu.
Then it occurred to the Venerable Ānanda:
“The Blessed One has commanded me:
‘Ānanda, prepare lodgings for this visiting bhikkhu. The Blessed One wishes to dwell in the same dwelling as that bhikkhu; the Blessed One wishes to dwell in the same dwelling as the Venerable Soṇa.
He prepared lodgings for the Venerable Soṇa in the very dwelling where the Blessed One was staying.
Then the Blessed One, having spent much of the night sitting in the open air, washed his feet and entered the dwelling.
The Venerable Soṇa also, having spent much of the night sitting in the open air, washed his feet and entered the dwelling.
Then the Blessed One, rising at the time of dawn, addressed the Venerable Soṇa:
“May it occur to you, monk, to speak the Dhamma.
“Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Soṇa replied to the Blessed One, and he recited all sixteen chapters of the Aṭṭhakavagga with his voice.
Then, at the conclusion of the Venerable Soṇa’s chanting, the Blessed One expressed his approval:

“Excellent, excellent, bhikkhu! You have well grasped, bhikkhu, these sixteen discourses of the Aṭṭhakavagga; you have well attended to them and well retained them. You are endowed with beautiful speech—articulate, flawless, and expressive of the meaning.
How many years have you been ordained, bhikkhu?
“I have been ordained for one year, Blessed One.”
“But why, monk, have you waited so long?
“For a long time, Bhante, I have seen the danger in sensual pleasures;
nevertheless, the life of a householder is cramped, full of many duties, and full of many tasks.”
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Having seen the danger in the world,
and having known the Dhamma that is free from acquisitions;”
The noble one does not delight in evil;
the pure one does not delight in evil.
Thus ends the sixth [verse].
